articles.content: The India-Palestine encounter in the AFC U-17 Asian Cup 2027 qualifiers was overshadowed by a major controversy after a Palestinian player appeared to make a racist gesture towards Indian captain Dallalmuon Gangte. The incident was captured on camera, but the referee did not take any action.The match was already becoming increasingly heated, with the Palestinian players repeatedly engaging in physical challenges and attempts to unsettle their Indian opponents. India, however, remained composed in a closely contested encounter as both sides fought for the top spot in the qualifying group.INDIAN FOOTBALL: FULL COVERAGEThe flashpoint came when Palestine's No. 19 was seen making a fanning-the-nose gesture close to Gangte. The action drew widespread criticism, with many interpreting it as a racist stereotype suggesting an unpleasant smell. Despite the incident being visible on the live broadcast, the match officials allowed play to continue without taking disciplinary action.There was another troubling moment involving Palestinian player Mohammed Jamhour. Around the ninth minute, Jamhour appeared to kick an Indian player twice from behind before stamping on his arm after the footballer had fallen to the ground. But this time, the referee stepped and issued a straight red card to the Palestine player.INDIA RESPOND WITH FOUR-GOAL PERFORMANCEWhile the incidents threatened to take attention away from the football, India's U-17 side delivered a commanding response on the pitch, registering a 4-1 victory.The Blue Colts made an early breakthrough through Kambouhao, who found the net in the seventh minute. Palestine managed to restore parity before the interval, with Yazan Khalifah converting a penalty to send the teams into the break level at 1-1. The contest also faced a temporary interruption due to heavy rain.India raised the tempo after the restart and regained the lead in the 51st minute. Mukundo produced a spectacular finish to put the Indian side ahead once again.The advantage grew just seven minutes later when captain Gangte got on the scoresheet, giving India some breathing room in the contest.Zoramdinthara then put the result beyond doubt with an 88th-minute goal, completing an emphatic 4-1 win for the Blue Colts. The Indian players celebrated a significant victory at the final whistle, having maintained their composure through a contest that was marred by controversial incidents.- Ends

articles.title: Abhishek Sharma pays tribute to Travis Head as Travishek era ends for SRH - India Today
articles.summary: Abhishek Sharma pays tribute to Travis Head as Travishek era ends for SRH India Today
articles.content: One of the most thrilling partnerships in the IPL won't be seen during the 2027 season. Travis Head and Abhishek Sharma won't be seen walking out together next year for Sunrisers Hyderabad after the Australian decided to pull out of the tournament to prioritise his international commitments.IPL 2027 RETENTION DAY HIGHLIGHTSSRH decided to release him ahead of next season, thus bringing an end to the fearsome Travishek partnership. Abhishek came into his own during the partnership with Head and decided to pay a heartwarming tribute on Tuesday, November 17.The Indian southpaw posted a simple message on his Instagram stories thanking Head for everything."Thank you Heady for everything," read the message from Abhishek.THE NUMBERS BEHIND TRAVISHEKDuring his 43 appearances for Sunrisers Hyderabad, Travis Head accumulated 1,351 runs at an average of 32.95 and an impressive strike rate of 176.14. However, his impact at the franchise was perhaps best reflected in the explosive partnership he built with Abhishek Sharma.The duo put together 1,892 runs across 42 innings, averaging 46.14, with six hundred-run stands and nine partnerships worth at least 50 runs. Only Shikhar Dhawan and David Warner have scored more runs as an opening pair for SRH. Head and Abhishek, though, hold a unique record: their run rate of 12.46 per over is the best in IPL history among partnerships that have accumulated 1,000 runs or more.Talking about his decision to skip IPL 2027, Head said that he wanted to prioritise better work-life balance for his family."After three incredible years with Sunrisers Hyderabad, I want to take a moment to say a heartfelt thank you to everyone who has been part of the journey," Head was quoted in a social media post shared by the franchise."This has been an extremely difficult decision, but with my ongoing international ambitions and the importance of finding a better work-life balance for my family, I feel it's the right one at this stage of my career.""I'm extremely proud of what we've achieved together and will always look back on my time at Sunrisers Hyderabad with great memories and appreciation," the left-handed batter said.SRH will be now tasked with finding Abhishek a new opening partner during the upcoming IPL 2027 auction on December 16.- Ends

articles.title: Drought-Hit Talukas In Maharashtra Rise To 308 - Deccan Chronicle
articles.summary: Drought-Hit Talukas In Maharashtra Rise To 308 Deccan Chronicle
articles.content: Mumbai: The Maharashtra government on Tuesday approved the declaration of drought in four more talukas — Chiplun, Dindori, Wada and Vikramgad — taking the total number of drought-affected talukas in the state to 308. Revenue Minister Chandrashekhar Bawankule directed officials to visit all districts before the Assembly session and submit a detailed assessment of drought conditions to the Chief Secretary. Surveys will also be conducted in 11 other talukas, including Hatkanangale, Gadhinglaj, Kagal and Karveer. Meanwhile, Rs 4,701.61 crore has been disbursed to 94.03 lakh farmers as drought relief as of November 16. Relief Minister Makarand Jadhav-Patil said eligible farmers facing technical issues related to e-KYC and Farmer IDs would also receive assistance.Chandrashekhar Bawankule, Revenue Minister and chairman of the Cabinet sub-committee on drought relief measures, held a meeting with ministers, including Agriculture Minister Dattatray Bharne, and senior officials, including Chief Secretary Rajesh Agrawal and Additional Chief Secretary of the Relief and Rehabilitation Department (RRD), Vinita Ved Singhal, at Mantralaya to discuss drought relief measures. Mr Bawankule also directed Guardian Secretaries to visit all districts before the winter session to assess the drought situation against official criteria and submit reports to the Chief Secretary. He also ordered a comprehensive survey of other talukas where drought has been demanded, including Hatkanangale, Gadhinglaj, Kagal and Karveer, with reports to be placed before the next meeting of the Cabinet sub-committee. Last month, the state government had declared 304 talukas drought-affected in two phases owing to deficient rainfall and crop damage. It has also extended 12 types of concessions to people in these drought-hit talukas. The RRD also issued a Government Resolution (GR) outlining the eligibility criteria for advance assistance of Rs 5,000 to farmers in the 304 drought-affected talukas during the 2026 kharif season. Officials said a GR listing 10 measures to tackle water scarcity would be issued within a day or two. The Finance Department has released Rs 83.18 crore for 212 schemes in 13 talukas under the Jal Jeevan Mission to ensure that tanker supplies can be avoided once the works are completed. An additional Rs 400 crore has been made available for retrofitting, while the pending Rs 349 crore for earlier water scarcity works is expected to be released through a supplementary demand by the end of December. Mr Bawankule directed that the number of agencies undertaking recharge shaft works be increased, quality standards be fixed and the necessary powers be given to Collectors. A senior official said that, so far, 96.74 lakh farmers in 304 talukas had been approved for advance assistance of Rs 5,000 each. Of these, 94.03 lakh farmers had received financial assistance. Another two to three lakh farmers are expected to receive the advance assistance in the next couple of days.

articles.title: India beat Pakistan 2-1 to clinch record 10th SAFF Championship title - Onmanorama
articles.summary: India beat Pakistan 2-1 to clinch record 10th SAFF Championship title Onmanorama
articles.content: India came from behind to beat arch-rivals Pakistan 2-1 in a thrilling final on Tuesday, clinching a record-extending 10th SAFF Championship title and their third consecutive crown. Fielding a second-string side, India overcame a first-half deficit to retain the title, with Sandip Mandi scoring a dramatic late winner in Dhaka. Pakistan took the lead in first-half stoppage time through Alamgir Ghazi, who curled a superb right-footed effort into the far corner in the 45+1st minute. India had struggled to find their rhythm in the opening half, with Pakistan dominating possession and creating more chances. Pakistan registered nine shots in the opening 30 minutes, including two on target, while India managed only two attempts, neither of which tested the goalkeeper. India had a flurry of opportunities around the 35th minute but failed to convert before Ghazi put Pakistan ahead. The match took a decisive turn in the 59th minute when Pakistan were reduced to 10 men. Junaid Shah was shown a straight red card following a VAR review for a rash tackle on Brison Fernandes. India made the numerical advantage count almost immediately, with Suhail Ahmad Bhat restoring parity in the 60th minute. Lhungdim Khaiminthang delivered a free-kick into the penalty area, and Macarton Nickson got a slight touch before Bhat side-footed the ball into the net. Both sides made changes as the contest entered its final stages. India brought on Abdul Rabeeh and Irfan Yadwad in the 72nd minute, and the substitutes combined to create another opportunity. Irfan's low cross found Rabeeh, whose first-time effort was blocked by the Pakistan defence. With extra time looming, India continued to press for a winner. Their persistence paid off in the 88th minute when Sandip Mandi rose to meet Rabeeh's outswinging corner and directed a powerful header downwards. The ball bounced towards the top corner, beyond the reach of Pakistan goalkeeper Yousuf Butt, sparking celebrations among the Indian players. The late strike sealed a memorable comeback for Naushad Moosa's side and ensured India retained their SAFF Championship crown. For Pakistan, who were appearing in their first-ever SAFF Championship final, it was a heartbreaking end to a campaign in which they had come close to claiming their maiden title.

implemented by the Maharashtra Pollution Control Board (MPCB) in collaboration with Emissions Market Accelerator, Environment and Climate Change Minister Pankaja Munde said..Follow The PSUWatch Channel on Whatsapp.Speaking at an event in Mumbai, Munde said the government wanted to develop, in collaboration with industries, solutions that balance environmental protection with economic development.Under the emissions trading scheme, participating industrial units will be given permits specifying their permissible sulphur dioxide emissions.Industries that can reduce emissions at a lower cost will be able to make additional reductions and sell their surplus permits, while those facing higher costs of emission reduction can purchase them, an official release said.Michael Greenstone, professor of economics at the University of Chicago, director of the Energy Policy Institute and co-chair of Emissions Market Accelerator, said research had shown that market-based schemes could achieve effective emission reductions while lowering the cost of pollution control for industries..The MPCB and the University of Chicago Trust also signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to use artificial intelligence and machine learning in environmental regulation and industrial inspections.The initiative will be implemented through the Energy Policy Institute at the University of Chicago India.Under the agreement, the two institutions will jointly develop and pilot an AI-based framework for environmental inspections..Follow PSU Watch on LinkedIN.BPCL holds workshop to scale up articles.summary: IIM Mumbai, Maharashtra Govt sign MoU to strengthen policy research PSU Watch
articles.content: New Delhi: The Indian Institute of Management (IIM) Mumbai on Tuesday said it has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Maharashtra government for strengthening public policy research, governance, and evidence-based decision-making..Follow The PSUWatch Channel on Whatsapp.The MoU, which covers 25 government policies and 26 schemes, aims to strengthen the interface between academic research and the government policymaking, enabling more effective implementation and evaluation of public schemes and policies, IIM Mumbai said in a statement..The agreement was signed during a two-day orientation programme of the Maharashtra Technical Assistance Cell (MahaTAC).The MoU was inked by IIM Mumbai Director Prof Manoj Kumar Tiwari and Ravi Jarande, Joint Secretary in the state Finance Department, in the presence of Dr Shrikar Pardeshi, Principal Secretary to Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis..MahaTAC was established through a joint initiative of the IIM Mumbai, the Centre for Research in Schemes and Policies (CRISP) and the Maharashtra government. It aims to bridge the gap between policy formulation and implementation through research, data-driven insights and actionable recommendations.The two-day orientation programme brought together policymakers, senior administrators, institutional leaders and academic experts to discuss governance, policy evaluation and institutional capacity building..Follow PSU Watch on LinkedIN.NISM, IICA sign MoU to strengthen corporate governance, ESG and capital markets.At the event, Pardeshi shared insights into the government's priorities, coordination among departments and governance, while Tiwari spoke about the importance of policy analytics, institutional research and evidence-based governance..(PSU Watch is India's Business News centre that places the spotlight on PSUs, Bureaucracy, Defence and Public Policy. 👉 Click to join our channel now: PSUWatch WhatsApp Channel. articles.summary: Indian sports wrap, November 17: Tanay, Sneha upset seeds, reach third round at Junior Badminton Nationals The Hindu
articles.content: CHENNAI BADMINTON Tanay, Sneha upset seeds, reach third round at Junior Badminton Nationals Rajasthan’s Sneha Lamba and Maharashtra’s Tanay Mehendale created early flutter in the 49th National Junior (U-19) badminton championships in Gangtok on Tuesday with straight-games upsets of much higher-ranked opponents. In girls’ singles, Sneha won 15-12, 15-6 against fourth seed Tanvi Reddy Andluri, who recently represented India in the World Junior Championships in Cairo, Egypt, while Tanay got the better of sixth seed Shaurya Mishra 15-13, 16-14 in boys’ singles. The seeds had got a bye in the opening round and all eyes were on the top stars to deliver on the second day of the individual competitions in Sikkim’s capital. While women’s top seed Shaina Manimuthu was pushed to three games by Maharashtra’s Naishaa Kaur Bhatoye, the Karnataka shuttler kept her nerves to win 15-9, 11-15, 15-5. Nishchal Anand, the top seed in boys’ singles, was also made to dig deep to beat Prangan Choudhury 15-11, 14-16, 15-10 in the second round. However, 11th and 13th seeds in boys’ singles were shown the door. Eleventh-seeded Sai Nachiketh Bhatraju lost 15-10, 9-15, 15-12 to Prince while 13th-seeded Harshad Shadish bowed out after a 15-12, 13-15, 15-9 defeat against Sparsh Sood. - Team Sportstar CRICKET Pakistan beats India by one wicket in last-ball thriller at Asia Cup Cricket for the Blind The much-anticipated India-Pakistan clash at the Asia Cup Cricket for the Blind 2026 lived up to its billing, producing a nail-biting finish as Pakistan secured a dramatic one-wicket victory off the final ball of the contest at Bashundhara Sports City, Dhaka. In a match that swung between the two sides, Pakistan chased down India’s challenging total of 179/6, finishing at 180/9 in 20 overs. - Team Sportstar ESPORTS Vanshaj Sharma wins Red Bull Wings Cup India, qualifies for World Final in Miami Vanshaj Sharma was crowned the Red Bull Wings Cup India National Champion after defeating Saransh Jain 2–0 in the best-of-three final at a packed Kettle Studio in Bengaluru on Sunday. The victory secured Sharma’s place at the Red Bull Wings Cup World Final in Miami, where he will represent India against national champions from around the world. Sharma won the opening game of the EA SPORTS FC 27 final 5–1 before sealing the title with a 4–1 victory in the second game. The straight-games result capped a dominant run through the eight-player knockout tournament, with Sharma winning all four games he played across the quarterfinals, semifinals and final. His campaign began with a 6–0 quarterfinal victory over Sharuk Sanjay. He followed that with a 10–2 win against Fadl Afridi in the semifinals, his highest-scoring performance of the evening, to book his place in the title decider. Across the tournament, Sharma scored 25 goals and conceded just four. Jain reached the final from the other half of the bracket, opening with a 9–2 win over Dhruv Keshwani before edging Rohit J Abraham 3–2 in the semifinals. His narrow semifinal victory set up the meeting with Sharma, who carried his scoring form into the championship contest and closed out the series without needing a third game. The remaining quarterfinals saw Rohit J Abraham defeat Satyam Jha 3–1, while Fadl Afridi progressed with a 4–0 victory over Akshay S. An exhibition clash between GodLike and Apex Gaming added another contest to the evening. Dobby and SMR represented GodLike, while Jonathan teamed up with Hydro for Apex Gaming. The Apex duo secured a comfortable 10–3 victory in the showmatch, which brought the two organisations together on the virtual football pitch. - Team Sportstar GOLF Ridhima takes lead in 15th Leg of WPGT, amateur Aida tied third with Vani and Tvesa Ridhima Dilawari made a confident start, carding a two-under 69 to take the opening-round lead at the 15th and final leg of the Women’s Pro Golf Tour at the Jaypee Wishtown Golf Course in Noida on Tuesday. Riya Jadon was just one stroke behind with a one-under 70, while amateur Aida Thimmaiah joined experienced professionals Vani Kapoor and Tvesa Malik at even-par 71. The opening round proved a demanding test for the field. Only two players managed under par scores, while three others returned even-par cards. The leader of the Order of Merit, Dilawari, continued to impress by picking up four birdies against two bogeys. Her four victories this year came at Kalhaar Blues & Greens, Poona Club, Jaypee Wishtown and Prestige Golfshire. She has also finished runner-up twice. She finished third in the 14th leg last week at the Rambagh Golf Club event behind the winner Jasmine Shekar and runner-up Vani. Jasmine has skipped the event as she is one of the six Indians playing in a Q-School event in Thailand. One of the encouraging performances of the day came from Bengaluru amateur golfer Aida, who had three birdies and three bogeys and on two occasions on the back nine she picked a birdie and immediately gave back the shot on the very next hole. Tvesa also finished at even par, although her round followed the opposite pattern. She was three-under 33 on the front nine including three birdies in a row from the seventh. She dropped three strokes on the back nine without any birdies to sign for 71. Tvesa has had a productive recent spell, finishing seventh at the Hero Women’s Indian Open with a one-under total of 287 (71-73-71-72). She has also recorded a domestic tour victory this season. Saanvi Somu, Lavanya Jadon and Sneha Singh were tied sixth at 1-over 72 and as many as nine players were tied for ninth place. The huge bunch included Shrestha Shukla, Mannat Brar, Prarthana Khanna, Shweta Mansingh, Jasmandeep Kaur, Yaalisai Verma, Sneha Sharan, Janneya Dasanniee and Agrima Manral. - PTI Saurav Rathi shoots 65 to take opening-round lead at Servo Masters Gurugram’s Saurav Rathi opened the new DP World PGTI season with a bang, firing an impressive seven-under 65 to take a two-shot lead after the first round of the Rs 1 crore IndianOil SERVO Masters Golf in Digboi, Assam, on Tuesday. Rathi, 24, made eight birdies and dropped his only shot on the par-4 18th, his closing hole, to emerge as the outright leader on a course where only 29 players in the 120-man field managed to break par. Delhi’s 21-year-old Anshul Kabthiyal and seasoned campaigner Om Prakash Chouhan shared second place at five-under 67. Rathi, a regular on the DP World PGTI since 2019, recently secured his full playing rights for the new season after finishing 17th at the DP World PGTI Qualifying Tournament Final Stage in Ahmedabad. Despite nursing a left-leg injury sustained after slipping on wet stairs at the course on Monday, Rathi hit 12 of 14 fairways and 15 greens in regulation. “It was a solid round and a good start to the new season. I was five-under after nine holes, made two more birdies on the 11th and 12th, followed by another birdie on the 14th. I made pars after that before dropping a disappointing bogey on the 18th from the middle of the fairway, just 40 yards out,” said Rathi. Chouhan, an 11-time winner on the DP World PGTI, a former winner on the European Challenge Tour and the 2023 DP World PGTI rankings champion, also carded a 67, making eight birdies against three bogeys. Four players shared fourth place at four-under 68, including Gurugram’s Kushal Singh, Pune’s Divyansh Dubey, Kapurthala’s Yuvraj Singh and Lucknow’s Sanjeev Kumar. Kushal made seven birdies and three bogeys, while Divyansh registered six birdies and two bogeys. Yuvraj recovered from a double-bogey on the par-5 15th and another bogey with seven birdies, while Sanjeev produced five birdies against a lone bogey. - PTI SQUASH Senthilkumar in Qatar squash semifinals Indian squash player Velavan Senthilkumar moved into the semifinals of the QSF 3 PSA Copper tournament with a straight-game victory over Egypt’s Omar Said in Doha, Qatar, on Tuesday. Second seed Senthilkumar, who won two PSA Copper-level titles this year, beat his fifth-seeded opponent 11-9, 11-1, 13-11 in the quarterfinals of the USD 40,500 prize money tournament for men. World No 38 Senthilkumar will next meet the winner of the quarterfinal between local challenger Abdulla Al-Tamimi and Malaysia’s Ameeshenraj Chandaran. -Team Sportstar

articles.title: Maharashtra approves Rs 16.74 crore VGF for Sindhudurg-Navi Mumbai flights - PSU Watch
articles.summary: Maharashtra approves Rs 16.74 crore VGF for Sindhudurg-Navi Mumbai flights PSU Watch
articles.content: New Delhi: The Maharashtra Government has approved Rs 16.74 crore in Viability Gap Funding (VGF) to run flights between Sindhudurg and Navi Mumbai for a year, replacing an earlier plan to link the coastal Konkan district with Mumbai airport, officials said..Follow The PSUWatch Channel on Whatsapp.To revive air services from Chipi airport in Sindhudurg district, known for its scenic shoreline, historic forts and lush green Western Ghats, the state cabinet on October 27 gave nod to 100 percent VGF for airlines operating on the Navi Mumbai-Chipi and Chipi-Navi Mumbai routes.The airport, located in Chipi village in Vengurla taluka of Sindhudurg district, was inaugurated in October 2021 to boost tourism and connectivity in the Konkan region.However, services at the airport had been suspended due to technical hurdles. The resumption of Chipi airport will greatly benefit tourists from Maharashtra and elsewhere, state Ports Minister Nitesh Rane had said..According to a Government Resolution (GR) issued by the General Administration Department on Monday, the funding has been sanctioned to M/s Just Udo Aviation Pvt Ltd (Fly 91) at the rate of Rs 6,200 per seat under the Centre's Regional Connectivity Scheme (RCS) guidelines.Earlier, on March 30 this year, the government approved Fly 91 to operate flights on the Chipi-Mumbai-Chipi route. However, the airline could not secure slots at the Mumbai airport. Following this, the Maharashtra Airport Development Company (MADC) proposed operating the flights on the Sindhudurg-Navi Mumbai-Sindhudurg route instead.The government has formally cancelled the March 30 approval for the Mumbai route and granted administrative and financial nod to spend Rs 16,74,62,000 for the Sindhudurg-Navi Mumbai sector, the officials said..As per the GR, the 100 percent VGF support will be valid for a period of one year from the date actual flight operations begin, or until the route is formally included and started under the central government's RCS-UDAN scheme, whichever is earlier. No extension will be granted beyond this one-year..Follow PSU Watch on LinkedIN.91% of Mumbai Airport's international traffic to remain unaffected as Terminal 1 is rebuilt.The government has also directed MADC to pursue the inclusion of the Sindhudurg-Navi Mumbai route under the Centre's RCS scheme. Additionally, MADC has been asked to hold discussions with Fly 91 to negotiate a possible reduction in the VGF rate, even though the Request for Proposal does not have a provision for negotiation.The VGF payments will be calculated and disbursed based on the actual frequency of flights operated on the route, the GR stated..(PSU Watch is India's Business News centre that places the spotlight on PSUs, Bureaucracy, Defence and Public Policy. 👉 Click to join our channel now: PSUWatch WhatsApp Channel. articles.content: Former India captain MS Dhoni has retired from playing with Chennai Super Kings in the Indian Premier League and will take up a new role as team mentor from the 2027 season. Dhoni was bought by the Super Kings in the inaugural IPL auction in 2008 and went on to guide the franchise to five IPL championships. The 45-year-old spent 17 out of 19 seasons with the Super Kings, also playing for Rising Pune Supergiant when the Chennai club were suspended. Dhoni finishes his IPL career with 5,439 runs and an average of 38.30 across 278 matches. "For nearly two decades, we have walked and grown alongside each other, through triumphs, setbacks and everything in between. "Dhoni will always be a part of our identity. This will always be his home." Dhoni, who hails from Ranchi, enjoys huge popularity in the southern Indian city of Chennai where ‌crowds throng stadia just to get a glimpse of their "Thala", the Tamil word for leader. Runs stopped flowing from his blade in recent years ‌but legions of his fans still filled the stands to watch Dhoni batting lower down the order. Even that was not possible this year, however, and Dhoni sat out the entire season with a calf strain, which effectively ⁠signalled the end of his career. Dhoni has been the ​face of the franchise since joining them in ​2008 and played two seasons with Rising Pune Super Giant ​only when Chennai were handed a two-year suspension following a corruption ⁠scandal. articles.summary: India captaincy as demanding as PM's job? Shubman Gill has a hilarious response India Today
articles.content: Shubman Gill was asked if captaining the Indian cricket team was as demanding as being the country's Prime Minister, given the enormous following cricket enjoys in India and the scrutiny that comes with leading the national side.The question came during an interaction at an event organised by the Indian High Commission in Wellington to commemorate 100 years of sporting ties between India and New Zealand on Tuesday. The host cited a popular joke in New Zealand that the Prime Minister's job was not the most pressurised in the country, with that distinction belonging to the captain of the All Blacks rugby team, before asking Gill if the same held true in India."Not much, you know, just keep winning," Gill quipped, drawing laughter from those present.The India captain was also asked about the expectations that come with succeeding some of the biggest names in Indian cricket as Test captain. Gill, who took over the leadership from Rohit Sharma in 2025, said he did not feel burdened by the legacy of his predecessors."I don't think I feel any weight of the expectations," he said."They paved the path for us and I think it's now our turn to walk on that path and take the learnings and their experiences."Gill also acknowledged the influence of senior players and the coaching staff in helping him navigate the responsibilities of leadership."We have been very fortunate to have someone like Virat Bhai or Rohit (Sharma) and even Gautam Bhai (Gautam Gambhir) for that matter, some of the really experienced players who have played all around the world and have had tremendous success. So their experiences, we value a lot," he added.Away from the demands of international cricket, Gill said New Zealand offered the Indian players an opportunity to unwind during a busy tour. He pointed out that several members of the squad enjoyed visiting cafes, grabbing coffee and going on walks without attracting too much attention.India, meanwhile, are preparing for a challenging two-Test series against New Zealand, which begins at the Basin Reserve in Wellington on November 19. The second Test will be played in Christchurch from November 27.FOUR-MAN PACE ATTACK?Gill confirmed on Tuesday that India were considering a four-pronged pace attack for the series opener, with Jasprit Bumrah returning to lead the bowling unit. The team are weighing their options, with Mohammed Siraj, Prasidh Krishna, Akash Deep and Anshul Kamboj among the other pace contenders. India are also expected to use one specialist spinner.Since taking over as Test captain, Gill has led India in 11 matches, winning six, losing three and drawing two. His first major assignment was the five-Test series in England in 2025, which India drew 2-2. He subsequently led India to a 2-0 home series victory over the West Indies. India have had a tough time on the road, having been held to a draw in Sri Lanka earlier this year.The New Zealand assignment will offer another test of Gill's leadership, particularly in conditions traditionally suited to seam bowling. India will need to win at least one, if not both the Tests in New Zealand, to ensure their chances of reaching the World Test Championships remain intact.- Ends
